transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess I’ve just been feeling really wound up lately. It’s not like anything dramatic is happening, but my body feels tense a lot of the time, like I’m bracing for something bad even when I’m just sitting at my desk… or even trying to relax and enjoy dance night. I’m probably not explaining it perfectly, but it’s been hard to shake.
Do you find that your anxiety is present most of the time, even when you're not in any particular stressful situation or thinking about something specific?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but it does feel like I’m wound up most of the time, even when nothing specific is going on. Like I’ll just be sitting at my desk, or I’ll be out at dance night trying to enjoy myself, and my body still feels like it’s bracing for the next bad thing. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself worrying about things more than you used to, or feeling anxious about different things happening in your life, even when there’s no clear reason for concern?

Yeah… I think it has spread out more than it used to. I mean, it’s not just one thing, like the condo stuff anymore. It kind of jumps around — like I’ll start wondering if my cousin is upset with me, or if I’m going to mess up on a support call at work, and then suddenly I’m thinking about money and whether I’m ever going to move forward in life.

I know some of that is normal to worry about, so I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is… but it does feel like my mind keeps finding new things to latch onto, even when there isn’t really a clear reason right then.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, fatigue, or trouble sleeping that seem to go along with this feeling of being wound up?

Yeah, mostly that wound-up feeling and tension, I think. Like my body is kind of braced all the time, even if I’m just sitting at my desk doing normal work, or even at dance night when I’m supposed to be relaxing and having fun. It’s not like I’m panicking or anything… I just feel physically on edge a lot. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you find it hard to control or stop the worrying, even when you know it might not make sense?

Yeah… I’d say that’s probably true. I can sometimes talk myself down a little, but it’s harder than I feel like it should be.

Like, even if I tell myself, “You already checked the spreadsheet,” or “You already sent that email,” my brain doesn’t really let it go. It’ll keep looping, and then one “what if” turns into five more before I can pull myself back. I know that probably sounds a little excessive… but that’s kind of what it feels like.
Do these feelings of worry and tension ever show up even when things are going smoothly in your life, or do they usually start only when something stressful is happening?

I think it can happen even when nothing major is going wrong, yeah. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like it’s constant or dramatic, but it doesn’t always need a real crisis to start.

Like, the condo situation was one thing, but now the worry kind of moves around. I’ll be having an otherwise normal day and suddenly I’m wondering if my cousin is upset with me, or if I’m going to mess up on a support call, or how I’m supposed to save enough money and actually move forward. It just… finds something, I guess. Does that make sense?
Have these feelings of ongoing worry and tension been present for most days over the past six months, even if they vary in intensity?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, not every single moment of every day, but most days, yes.

It’s been going on for maybe about nine months now, since the condo loan started moving toward foreclosure. I kept thinking once that got clearer or once I adjusted, it would settle down, but it’s kind of stayed in the background. Does that count as what you’re asking?
